name: Shaphat
overview: Shaphat was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the son of Shecaniah. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes or significant narrative attached to his character. His presence is recorded in the genealogical context, emphasizing his lineage within Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Shaphat is a proper name meaning 'he judges.' This meaning reflects a common Hebrew root related to judgment, although the name itself was not given by God. The name highlights a characteristic associated with discernment or decision-making.
familyAndRelationships: Shaphat is explicitly identified as the son of Shecaniah. Additionally, he is noted as the father of Shemaiah. Beyond these relationships, Scripture does not provide further family details.
scriptureSignificance: Shaphat's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:22. His mention contributes to the biblical record of the lineage from which important figures of Israel emerged. While not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion affirms the meticulous preservation of God's covenant people through generations.
